topics.label: Canada Immigration Document Checklist
topics.seoTitle: Canada Immigration Document Checklist | Free Tool
topics.metaDescription: Build a Canada immigration document checklist for your application — identity, education, language, work, funds and family records.
topics.lead: Most refusals and delays trace back to documentation: a missing police certificate, an unverified credential, an incomplete employment reference. This free tool helps assemble a document checklist tailored to the application you are preparing — identity and civil documents, education credentials and assessments, language test results, work experience evidence, proof of funds, medical and police certificates, and family records. Requirements differ by program, so the checklist is a starting point, not a substitute for program-specific instructions.

topics.label: Free Canada Immigration Assessment
topics.seoTitle: Free Canada Immigration Assessment | Commonwealth Migration
topics.metaDescription: Request a free Canada immigration assessment from a CICC-regulated RCIC and get a clear read on the pathways that fit your profile.
topics.lead: A free assessment is a structured first look at your profile: your goal, current status, education, language ability, work history, family situation and any prior applications or refusals. A licensed RCIC uses it to identify which Canadian immigration pathways are realistically open to you, what evidence would be needed, and what the sensible next step is. There is no cost and no obligation, and no outcome is guaranteed.

topics.label: Book an Immigration Consultation in Canada
topics.seoTitle: Book an Immigration Consultation in Canada | CMG
topics.metaDescription: Book a consultation with a licensed RCIC in Brampton, Ontario or by phone and video anywhere in Canada — clear advice on your next immigration step.
topics.h1: Book an Immigration Consultation in Canada
topics.lead: Booking a consultation with a licensed RCIC gives you a focused, personalised conversation about your Canadian immigration options. Consultations are available in person at the Brampton, Ontario office and by phone or video for clients across Canada and abroad. Bring identity and status documents, education and language records, work history, family details and any prior refusal or procedural fairness letter so the discussion can be specific rather than generic.

topics.label: Pay for Your Immigration Consultation
topics.seoTitle: Pay for Your Immigration Consultation | Commonwealth Migration
topics.metaDescription: Securely pay for your Commonwealth Migration consultation or service fee — Canadian immigration guidance from licensed RCICs.
topics.lead: Commonwealth Migration Group Inc. provides a secure online payment step for consultations and agreed service fees. Payment confirms a booked consultation or an agreed engagement; it does not purchase an immigration outcome. Clients should always verify the licence status of any representative on the CICC Public Register before paying for immigration advice.

topics.label: Canada Immigration Blog & Guides
topics.seoTitle: Canada Immigration Blog & Guides | Commonwealth Migration
topics.metaDescription: Practical Canada immigration guides and explainers — Express Entry, work and study permits, family sponsorship, visitor visas and current news.
topics.lead: The Commonwealth Migration blog publishes practical, plain-language guides to Canadian immigration: how Express Entry draws and CRS scores work, work and study permit requirements, family sponsorship and super visas, provincial nominee programs, and what to do after a refusal. Articles are written for people doing their own research and link to the official sources that matter.

topics.label: Canada Immigration News
topics.seoTitle: Canada Immigration News & Updates | Commonwealth Migration
topics.metaDescription: Track Canada immigration news — Express Entry draw results, program changes, policy updates and what they mean for applicants.
topics.lead: Canadian immigration rules move quickly: draw sizes and CRS cut-offs shift, category-based selection changes which occupations are invited, and provincial programs open and pause without much notice. This news hub collects the updates that actually affect applicants and explains what each change means in practice, with links to the official announcements.

topics.label: Express Entry Draws
topics.seoTitle: Express Entry Draws | Latest CRS Cut-Offs & Results
topics.metaDescription: Track the latest Express Entry draw results — CRS cut-offs, invitations issued, draw categories and program rounds, updated as IRCC publishes them.
topics.lead: Express Entry draws are the rounds in which IRCC invites the highest-ranked candidates to apply for permanent residence. Each draw has a date, a category or program, a CRS cut-off and a number of invitations issued. Following the pattern of recent draws is the most practical way to judge how competitive your own CRS score currently is, and whether a category-based round or a provincial nomination is the faster route.
headings: What the Cut-Off Means For You
